user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure you have admin access to both SVN and Git servers
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

```bash
# Backup SVN repo
svnadmin dump /path/to/svn/repo > svn_backup.dump
```

---

## Morning: Preparation (2–3 hours)

### Step 1 — Install Tools
```bash
# Install git-svn
sudo apt install git-svn        # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install git-svn            # macOS

# Verify
git svn --version
```

### Step 2 — Map SVN Authors to Git Authors
SVN uses usernames; Git needs name + email.

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors
svn log --quiet svn://your-repo-url | \
  grep -E "^r[0-9]+" | \
  awk '{print $3}' | \
  sort -u > authors.txt
```

Create `authors-transform.txt`:
```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
deploy = Deploy Bot <deploy@company.com>
```

### Step 3 — Understand Your SVN Layout

| Layout Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Standard** | Has `/trunk`, `/branches`, `/tags` |
| **Non-standard** | Custom folder structure |

---

## Late Morning: Clone SVN → Git (1–2 hours)

### Option A — Standard Layout
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors-transform.txt \
  my-git-repo
```

### Option B — Non-Standard Layout
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --trunk=trunk \
  --branches=branches \
  --tags=releases \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  my-git-repo
```

> ⏱️ **Time varies** — small repos: minutes | large history: 1–2 hours

---

## Early Afternoon: Clean Up the Repo (1 hour)

```bash
cd my-git-repo

# Convert SVN branches to Git branches
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/origin \
  --format='%(refname:short)' | \
  grep -v '@' | while read branch; do
    git branch "$branch" "refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
  done

# Convert SVN tags to proper Git tags
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/origin/tags \
  --format='%(refname:short)' | while read tag; do
    git tag "${tag#tags/}" "refs/remotes/origin/$tag"
    git branch -d -r "origin/$tag" 2>/dev/null || true
  done

# Remove SVN remote tracking refs
git for-each-ref refs/remotes --format='%(refname:short)' | \
  while read ref; do
    git branch -d -r "$ref" 2>/dev/null || true
  done

# Clean up SVN metadata
rm -rf .git/svn
```

### Verify the result
```bash
git log --oneline -10        # Check commit history
git branch -a                # Check branches
git tag                      # Check tags
```

---

## Mid Afternoon: Push to Git Remote (30 min)

```bash
# Add your new Git remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/org/my-git-repo.git

# Push everything
git push origin --all        # All branches
git push origin --tags       # All tags
```

---

## Late Afternoon: Validate & Team Onboarding (1–2 hours)

### Validation Checklist
- [ ] Commit count matches SVN (`svn log --quiet | grep -c "^r"`)
- [ ] All branches present
- [ ] All tags present
- [ ] Latest code matches SVN HEAD
- [ ] Author names/emails look correct

```bash
# Quick diff check between SVN HEAD and Git HEAD
svn export svn://your-repo-url svn-export
git clone https://github.com/org/my-git-repo.git git-export
diff -rq --exclude=".git" --exclude=".svn" svn-export git-export
```

### Team Onboarding
Send this to every developer:

```bash
# Each developer runs:
git clone https://github.com/org/my-git-repo.git
cd my-git-repo

# Set identity (if not globally set)
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@company.com"
```

---

## End of Day: Cutover

- [ ] **Archive/lock** the SVN repository (set it to read-only)
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines to point to Git
- [ ] Update any documentation referencing SVN URLs
- [ ] Send team announcement — Git is now the source of truth

```bash
# Lock SVN (prevent future commits)
svnadmin lock /path/to/svn/repo
# or set pre-commit hook to reject all commits
```

---

## Timeline Summary

| Time | Task |
|---|---|
| 08:00–09:00 | Install tools, extract authors |
| 09:00–11:00 | Clone SVN repo to Git |
| 11:00–12:00 | Clean up branches/tags |
| 12:00–13:00 | Lunch break |
| 13:00–13:30 | Push to remote |
| 13:30–15:00 | Validate & diff check |
| 15:00–16:30 | Team onboarding & docs |
| 16:30–17:00 | Lock SVN, announce cutover |

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Unknown author error | Add missing user to `authors-transform.txt` |
| SSL certificate error | Add `--no-verify-ssl` flag |
| Slow clone | Use `--revision HEAD:1` to limit history |
| Merge commits missing | Use `git svn rebase` before final push |
| Binary files corrupted | Check SVN `svn:mime-type` properties |

---

> 💡 **Tip:** For very large repos (10k+ commits), consider running the clone overnight and doing cleanup + cutover the next morning.

Based on the migration plan above, the top 3 risks are:

---

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🕒 Clone Takes Longer Than Expected
**Why it happens:** `git svn clone` replays every commit one by one. A repo with thousands of commits or large binary files can take **hours longer than anticipated**, blowing the 1-day window.

**Mitigation:**
- Do a **test clone the night before** to get a realistic time estimate
- Use `--revision` to limit history depth if full history isn't needed

---

### 2. 👤 Incomplete Author Mapping
**Why it happens:** Any SVN username missing from `authors-transform.txt` causes the **entire clone to abort**, forcing a restart from scratch.

**Mitigation:**
- Extract and verify the full author list **before** starting the clone
- Use `--authors-prog` as a fallback to handle unknown authors automatically rather than stopping

---

### 3. 🔀 History or Branch Loss
**Why it happens:** Non-standard SVN layouts, copied branches, or SVN `svn:mergeinfo` properties don't translate cleanly to Git, leading to **missing branches, flat history, or broken tags.**

**Mitigation:**
- Audit SVN structure beforehand (`svn ls svn://repo/`)
- Run the **diff validation step** before locking SVN
- Keep SVN in **read-only mode** (not deleted) for 2–4 weeks as a fallback

---

> ⚠️ **The biggest overall risk:** Locking SVN before validation is complete. Always validate first, cut over second.

## Pre-Cutover Checklist

- [ ] SVN commits frozen / team notified
- [ ] Full SVN backup completed
- [ ] All authors mapped in `authors-transform.txt`
- [ ] Test clone done to estimate timing
- [ ] Git remote created and accessible
- [ ] Clone completed without errors
- [ ] Commit count matches SVN
- [ ] All branches and tags present in Git
- [ ] Diff check passes (SVN HEAD vs Git HEAD)
- [ ] CI/CD pipelines updated
- [ ] Team cloned repo and confirmed access
- [ ] SVN set to read-only (**not deleted**)
- [ ] Cutover announced to team

## Rollback Option

**Keep SVN in read-only mode for 2–4 weeks after cutover.**

If anything goes wrong post-migration, revert by:
1. Unlocking SVN to accept commits again
2. Notifying the team to switch back to their SVN working copies
3. Discarding any Git-only commits made after cutover

> ✅ This is why you **never delete the SVN repo immediately** — it is your safety net until the team is fully settled on Git.

## One Prerequisite

**`git-svn` must be installed on the machine running the migration.**

Without it, no part of the clone process can begin.

```bash
# Verify it's installed
git svn --version
```

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
## Fastest Validation Step

**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN commit count
svn log --quiet svn://your-repo-url | grep -c "^r"

# Git commit count
git rev-list --count HEAD
```

> ✅ If the numbers match, your history migrated cleanly — takes less than **30 seconds** to run.
**08:00 Freeze SVN → 09:00 Clone → 11:00 Clean up → 13:00 Push → 14:00 Validate → 16:00 Lock SVN → 17:00 Done.**

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
## Two Tools

1. **`git-svn`** — clones SVN history into Git, preserving commits, branches, and tags.
2. **`svnadmin`** — backs up and locks the SVN repository before and after migration.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
## Final Cutover Approval

**The project or team lead** should approve the final cutover, confirming that:
- Validation checks have passed
- The whole team is aware and ready
- There is no critical work in progress that depends on SVN

> ✅ One named person — not the migration engineer themselves — should give explicit sign-off before SVN is locked.

## Communication Tip

**Send one clear message to the whole team before migration day stating the exact time SVN will be locked and the Git remote URL they will need** — so no one is caught off guard or left unable to work.

## Final Recap

| Step | Key Point |
|---|---|
| **Prepare** | Freeze SVN, back up, map all authors |
| **Clone** | Use `git-svn`, test timing beforehand |
| **Clean up** | Convert branches and tags properly |
| **Validate** | Match commit counts, diff check HEAD |
| **Cut over** | Get lead approval, lock SVN, push to Git |
| **Communicate** | Notify team early with Git URL and timeline |
| **Rollback** | Keep SVN read-only for 2–4 weeks |
| **Top risk** | Never lock SVN before validation is complete |

> ✅ A small repo can be fully migrated in one day if preparation is done the night before and the whole team is aligned from the start.

- Freeze SVN the night before
- Map all authors before cloning
- Use `git-svn` to clone
- Clean up branches and tags
- Validate commit counts
- Get lead approval before cutover
- Lock SVN, push to Git
- Keep SVN read-only for 2–4 weeks as fallback
